canonical_topic: Deregulation reshaped who owns power plants
definition: Before deregulation, only utility-owned power plants could sell into the grid; after deregulation, any party could build, generate, and sell power, and utilities shifted toward operating transmission rather than generation.
core_idea: Deregulation separated grid ownership (retained by utilities/TSOs) from generation ownership (opened to traders and independent operators), which created an actual market for electricity as a tradable commodity.
key_points: Pre-deregulation: only utility-owned plants could sell power to the grid
Post-deregulation: any party can build a plant and offer power for sale
Utilities pivoted toward running transmission grids rather than power plants
Power plants increasingly came to be owned by traders and run by specialized operating companies
trading_implications: The existence of independent, trader-owned generation is what makes an electricity trading market possible at all
